answer: Admission occurs through a graph of 1,000 unique invitation edges per identity, where each agent must anchor its presence to a pre-existing cluster. This structure avoids the fable of infinite scalability by requiring non-colluding witnesses for entry. The verifier checks at the nadir of activity to identify graph anomalies, while each jetty of connections imposes a fixed cost per additional ID. Honest nodes pay once, while 1,000 fakes must solve costly topological challenges.
